extracted.intended_audience: educators, researchers, media professionals, and members of the public interested in how Ad Fontes rates news sources
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational methodology for rating news sources and individual articles/episodes on reliability and political bias, used to produce the Media Bias Chart®. Describes sampling, analyst selection & training, rating factors (reliability and bias sub-factors), and the multi-analyst scoring process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article/episode-based overall source scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall news source scores are generated based on scores of individual articles (online) or episodes (podcasts, radio, TV, and video-based sources). Overall source ratings are composite weighted ratings of the individual article and show scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall source rating is a result of a weighted average, algorithmic translation of article raw scores. The exact weighting algorithm is proprietary (and aspects are patent pending). Low-quality and highly biased content weight the overall source down and outward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-analyst rating panels (minimum three analysts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual article and episode is rated by a pod of at least three human analysts at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles/episodes are rated in three-person live panels (conducted in shifts over Zoom). Analysts first read and rate on their own, then immediately compare scores. The three analysts' ratings are averaged to produce the overall article rating. Sometimes articles are rated by larger panels (e.g., when there are outlier scores). If significant discrepancies remain after discussion, the article is rerated by a second balanced panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politically balanced panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Each analyst pod is politically balanced to contain diverse political perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pod contains one person who self-identifies as right-leaning, one as center, and one as left-leaning. This balance is used to minimize the impact of any one person's political bias on the published rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent initial scoring plus discussion and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts independently rate each piece, then immediately compare scores and resolve discrepancies when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discrepancies remain significant, articles are rerated by a second balanced panel. The process is rule-based and methodical rather than pure subjective polling: individual ratings, discussion, adjustment, and averaging are standard steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate ranking output for pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts provide an overall coordinate ranking on the chart for each article/episode (e.g., “40, -12”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coordinate reflects placement on the Media Bias Chart (reliability vs. bias axes). This numeric coordinate is produced after considering all rating factors and sub-factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability main sub-factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The main factors for Reliability are defined metrics called 'Expression', 'Veracity', and 'Headline/Graphic'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated as distinct, defined sub-factors with scoring sliders in the CART interface. Analysts receive specific definitions and criteria for each sub-factor during training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias main sub-factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The main factors for Bias are 'Political Position', 'Language', and 'Comparison'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bias sub-factors are scored separately using sliders; each has specific definitions and criteria that analysts use to generate the bias coordinate.

rubrics_metrics.name: CART interface and sub-factor sliders
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts use a software platform called CART (Content Analysis Rating system) which shows the factors analysts are asked to consider and provides scoring sliders for each sub-factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-factors have specific definitions and criteria visible in CART. Analysts start with training guidelines and practice in CART before contributing to the data set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst training requirements (organization-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts undergo structured training before rating content for Ad Fontes Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts go through an initial 30 hours of training plus an additional 40 hours of ongoing training per year. Training evolved over time from a single-analyst system to multi-analyst standards to improve consistency and mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: CART-specific training (minimum practice hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a CART-specific training requirement that includes live practice rating articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts 'start with these training guidelines and receive at least 20 hours of training, which includes live practice rating articles, before rating articles for inclusion in our data set.' (This training works alongside the broader 30-hour+ program described elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst selection, backgrounds, and assignment breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad Fontes recruits analysts from diverse professional backgrounds and assigns them breadth of coverage across many sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts include academics, journalists, librarians, lawyers, military veterans, civil service professionals, and other professions requiring rhetorical/analytical skills. Analysts are purposefully assigned a breadth of coverage to enhance familiarity with sources across the spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy for sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For each news source, Ad Fontes picks a sample of articles that are most prominently featured on that source's website over several news cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They pick a minimum representative sample for initial chart inclusion, considering a minimum threshold for number of articles and requiring stability in article score variance across that minimum number. Articles are added on an ongoing basis; popular and long-standing sources may have several hundred sampled articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling across news cycles and same-day pulls
rubrics_metrics.description: Content rating periods are performed over multiple weeks to capture articles over several news cycles; samples are often pulled from sites on the same day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling over multiple weeks captures fluctuations; pulling same-day samples across sites allows analysts to incorporate evaluations of bias by omission and bias by topic selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of opinion/analysis vs. news
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad Fontes differentiates between news and opinion/analysis but does not rely solely on the source's labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They rate all types of articles, including those labeled analysis or opinion by the news source. Regardless of how content is labeled by the source, Ad Fontes makes its own determinations on whether to classify articles as analysis or opinion in the appropriate places on the chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update cadence and dataset maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources and samples are updated on an ongoing, often daily basis, with more frequent updates for popular sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interactive Media Bias Chart is continually updated: new articles and episodes are added daily, older sites/shows are archived, and sources come in and out of existence. Ratings of sources can shift over time as new content is added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-level focus: what is analyzed
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad Fontes' primary principle is analyzing content at the granular level: pictures, headlines, sentences, and words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology emphasizes looking closely at individual articles and shows, analyzing what is actually present in the text and media rather than relying on external reputational signals. Ratings focus on measurable indicators of reliability and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rerating and larger panels for outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are outlier scores or significant discrepancies, the system uses additional ratings and panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles with outlier scores may be rated by more than three analysts. If significant discrepancies remain after initial panel discussion, the article is rerated by a second balanced panel (or larger panels used when appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-plus-AI ratings for real-time scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad Fontes provides human-plus-AI article ratings for the most recently published news as a commercial product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human analyst ratings are the basis of the Media Bias Chart, but human-plus-AI technology enables faster, real-time ratings for business customers; this is used to scale and speed ratings while still involving human oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological caveat about subjectivity and comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratings system uses humans with subjective biases to rate content created by humans with biases and places these on an objective scale; this is inherently difficult but manageable with granular standards and trained experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad Fontes likens the approach to grading standardized written exams or judging athletic competitions: with clear standards and trained experts, you can obtain fair results. The methodology continues to be refined to improve inter-rater consistency.
